items.direction: Narrate this as a YouTube geography video comparing the GTA 6 game map with real Miami. The Narrator is a confident tour guide with a smirk: a warm, witty friend showing you around Miami, quietly amused by how much Rockstar copied. Conversational, relaxed but energetic, with dry humour; never shouty, never hyped-gamer, never slow documentary. The opening bet ('I bet you a hundred dollars') is a playful, low, slightly cinematic challenge, like the start of an 80s crime movie, then the voice brightens into the tour. Before each reveal of a game name (Ocean Beach, the Cortez, Hotel Dixon, the Colon Hotel) take a tiny half-second 'watch this' pause, then land the name with a grin. Absurd facts are delivered deadpan, so the fact is the joke. Stress the key words naturally. Pace about 160 words per minute, short crisp pauses between sentences. Accent: native General American English, neutral American accent from first word to last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy throughout. Say 'GTA six' as the letters G, T, A then 'six'. Pronounce 'Cortez' as 'cor-TEZ', 'Colon' exactly like the punctuation mark 'colon' (KOH-lun), never 'Colonna', 'Leonida' as 'lee-oh-NEE-dah'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word: stop right after the final sentence and never add, invent or continue with any words of your own.
lines: I bet you a hundred dollars you've already seen the GTA six map. Because Rockstar didn't invent Vice City. They copied it. From Miami. A hotel strip, copied right down to the palm trees. An apartment building that doesn't exist anymore... except in the game. A swamp, a sugar town, a giant lobster that turned into a whale. And mountains, in a state whose highest point is 105 metres. GTA six launches November 19th. So let's put the trailers next to the real map. And at the end, I'll show you the moment Miami started copying the game back. Grab a controller. And a map of Florida. Ten stops. Stop one. Ocean Drive, Miami Beach. Pastel Art Deco hotels, neon signs, palm trees, and the beach right across the road. In the trailers, it's called Ocean Beach. Same strip. Same pastel colours. The Colony Hotel becomes the Cortez. Hotel Victor becomes Hotel Dixon. And here's the thing. Rockstar has copied this street before. In 2002's Vice City, that same Colony Hotel was the "Colon" Hotel. Same building. Copied twice. Twenty-four years apart. That hotel is still standing. But a few blocks away, two towers are slowly going down.
